data.name: SettingsLifetimesHeading
data.comment: Settings → Intel section heading: how long each kind of intel counts as current.

data.name: SettingsLifetimesNote
data.value: Each kind of news counts as current for this long after it was reported, fading as it ages; then it drops off the panels and the map. Shared by every PC on this database. "No visual" is a flag on a sighting, not a lifetime of its own.
data.comment: Settings → Intel, under the lifetimes heading.

data.comment: Settings → Intel lifetime row: a pilot placed by being the victim of a killmail.

data.name: SettingsMinutes

data.name: SettingsSeconds

data.name: SettingsKm

data.name: SettingsFollowUpHeading
data.comment: Settings → Intel section heading: lines that add to an earlier report.

data.name: SettingsFollowUpNote
data.value: A line with no system of its own ("+2", "nv", "clr") adds to the same reporter's last report in the same channel when it comes within this time.
data.comment: Settings → Intel, under the follow-up heading. The quoted words are what people type in intel channels; keep them as they are.

data.name: SettingsFollowUpWindow
data.comment: Settings → Intel number box label.

data.name: SettingsCampHeading
data.comment: Settings → Intel section heading: gate camps worked out from killmails.

data.name: SettingsCampNote
data.value: Kills on one gate, each soon after the one before and sharing an attacker, are a camp once enough different pilots have been lost there. A single kill is not a camp.
data.comment: Settings → Intel, under the gate camp heading.

data.name: SettingsCampGateKm
data.value: Within this distance of a gate
data.comment: Settings → Intel number box label: how near a stargate a kill must be.

data.name: SettingsCampWindow
data.comment: Settings → Intel number box label.

data.name: SettingsCampVictims
data.value: Pilots lost before it is a camp
data.comment: Settings → Intel number box label: how many different pilots must be lost.

data.name: SettingsStandingsHeading
data.comment: Settings → Intel section heading.

data.name: SettingsStandingsNote
data.value: Pilots are coloured by the standings of the character looking: the one a panel follows, or the nearest online character. Personal contacts come first, then the corporation's, then the alliance's. Choose a character here to use its standings everywhere instead.
data.comment: Settings → Intel, under the standings heading.

data.name: SettingsStandingsFrom

data.name: SettingsStandingsEachClient
data.comment: First choice of the Standings from picker: no character forced.

data.name: SettingsDistanceHeading
data.comment: Settings → Intel section heading.

data.name: SettingsDistanceNote
data.value: How near a threat is counts stargates and every open Thera and Turnur connection, both ways. Travel distances can also count our own jump bridges, the ways the character's alliance may use.
data.comment: Settings → Intel, under the distance heading. Thera and Turnur are system names; keep them.

data.name: SettingsUseBridges
data.value: Use our jump bridges in travel distances
data.comment: Settings → Intel check box.

data.name: SettingsAlertsHeading
data.comment: Settings → Intel section heading: numbers shared by every intel alarm.

data.name: SettingsAlertsNote
data.value: Shared by every intel alarm. Only news this new fires an alarm and lights up a panel row; what was already there is not said, and older news is still shown.
data.comment: Settings → Intel, under the intel alarms heading.

data.name: SettingsFresh

data.name: SettingsFeedWarningHeading

data.name: SettingsFeedWarningNote
data.value: The Intel tool warns when zKillboard is not reading every kill in New Eden: kills anywhere else then never reach intel. The warning can be dismissed there, for every PC.
